findings.location: scripts/native_qualification_v3.py check_capture (exe rule) and check_qualification (no cross-capture file-identity rule); vectors.json positive[0..3] captures EFFECT_GATE process.exe, files and executableMaps; README 'What v3 changes' P1 running-image row
findings.finding: The new process-image rule compares /proc/<pid>/exe (device, inode) only with the same capture's observation of the image path. Nothing ties a (device, inode) to one path and one content across the bundle's captures, or within one capture. All four positives (inherited from v2, now load-bearing) report the gate executable and the Python interpreter at the same file: the EFFECT_GATE capture gives harness-effect-gate (sha ...a001) device 123, inode 2004, and its exe is (123, 2004). The SERVER and WORKER captures give python3.12 (sha 5555...) at the same (123, 2004). So the accepted positives themselves carry an observation that the gate's running image is the interpreter's inode, which is the P1 condition, and one inode cannot hold two fs-verity contents. Probe A: setting the gate's file, map and exe to the broker capture's broker-binary inode (123, 2002) is ACCEPTED by check_qualification. Probe A3: SERVER's script and python3.12 at one inode in one capture are also ACCEPTED. An honest inspector would catch a real hard link through the content digest, so this is an impossible-observation-set gap of the round-3 P4 kind, not an open native path. But it is the evidence v3 adds for P1, and the positives contradict it.
findings.requiredChange: In check_qualification, require across all role captures (and within each one) that every observed (device, inode) names exactly one path with one content digest and verity, and every path one (device, inode); exe is then covered. Give the gate's file its own inode in the positives, and add negatives for probes A and A3.

findings.location: scripts/native_qualification_v3.py check_migration and module docstring (line 19 'the v1-nonce scan'); README 'Migration from v2' ('v2's v1-to-v2 rules, one version later'); vectors.json M01-M09
findings.finding: v3 migration only sees v2 history, and v1 history drops out. A host enrolled under v1 that never enrolled v2 truthfully attests an empty v2 history. Its v3 record is then ACCEPTED on the same boot as its v1 record, reusing the v1 run and capacity nonces (probe: v1 positive 1's bootId 12345678-...-9abc and nonces unit-nonce/unit-capacity-nonce, no_v2_history=True). The reviewed W01 resolution requires a maintenance reboot and a fresh, non-reused generation for every enrollment (§4.4: migration 'never reuses a v1 generation or nonce'; §5.5 M3). After a full v2 history, a v3 run nonce equal to a v1 nonce is also ACCEPTED. v2 enforced both against v1, so v2's migration guarantee no longer holds for hosts with v1 history. The model docstring still claims a v1-nonce scan.
findings.requiredChange: Make check_migration take the host's complete retained history of every earlier version: v1 records under the pinned v1 schema and v2 records under the pinned v2 schema. Refuse a shared boot ID and any earlier nonce in v3 data. Alternatively, refuse a host with v1 history and no v2 history, and still scan v1 nonces. Restate caller obligation 2 for both versions, fix the docstring, and add M-vectors for v1-to-v3 and for v1-nonce reuse.

findings.location: qualification.schema.json $defs.capture.cgroupMembers items (no exe); scripts/native_qualification_v3.py check_capture WORKER branch; README P1 rows and decision 1
findings.finding: The image is observed only for the inspected process. WORKER co-members, which are descendants of the worker, carry no exe, so their images, whether another role's binary or any other executable, are not observed. Interpreted roles (SERVER and WORKER) share python3.12 as their image, and nothing observes which script the interpreter runs. A SERVER process running the worker's script, or any script outside its closure, therefore gives the same capture. The rows do not claim more, but 'Only the role's own executable may appear in its closure' is a statement about the declared closure, not about the code that runs.
findings.requiredChange: Add exe to member rows and require the role's image for every WORKER member, or state that descendant images rest on SELinux entrypoints (W02e) and the worker filter (W02d). State that for interpreted roles the script is declared, not observed.

findings.location: scripts/native_qualification_v3.py check_record native-only rule (interpreter_content); README P1 closure row
findings.finding: 'Native-only' is defined only against the enrolled interpreter executable, by path or content. Two probes on positive 1, with bundles fully rebound, were ACCEPTED by check_qualification. In the first, /opt/planeon/python/3.12.14/lib/libpython3.12.so.1.0 is listed and mapped by SERVER, WORKER and EFFECT_GATE. In the second, an unenrolled /opt/planeon/python/3.11.9/bin/python3.11 is listed and mapped by EFFECT_GATE and OBSERVER. A native-only gate can therefore map the Python runtime library (A05 shared-library allowance) and run embedded Python. Exploiting this needs the gate's own enrolled binary to do so, so the risk is low.
findings.requiredChange: Either mark the interpreter's runtime closure (libpython and extension modules) in the interpreted roles' closures and refuse it, and any other interpreter binary, in native-only closures, or state that native-only constrains only the process image and the enrolled interpreter file.

findings.location: scripts/native_qualification_v3.py check_capture pids.current rule; README P6 row
findings.finding: pids.current is charged per task in cgroup_can_fork, which runs for every copy_process, threads included. It is uncharged only in release_task, through pids_release. cgroup_exit removes an exited task from cgroup.procs, and Threads: counts live threads. A worker cgroup holding an exited but unreaped child therefore has a pids.current one above its listed members' total. The probe (WORKER pidsCurrent 3 for 2 single-thread members) is refused with 'task count differs from pids.current or exceeds pids.max'. That is a transient refusal of a legitimate host. The README's 'counts tasks' is correct; equality also needs the inspector to read a quiescent (frozen and reaped) cgroup.
findings.requiredChange: State the inspector obligation (read with the cgroup frozen and no unreaped children), or record zombie members, or allow pids.current minus the member total to equal a reported zombie count.

findings.location: README K1 statement and K1 row; scripts/native_qualification_v3.py check_record boot-entry rules and _boot_entry; vectors.json positive bootEntries
findings.finding:
Four points narrow the K1 statement.
(a) The ENROLLED and MAINTENANCE labels are declared data. Swapping the command lines, so the enrolled entry carries systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target, is ACCEPTED. Nothing ties the entries to the installed loader configuration.
(b) systemd-boot exports LoaderEntrySelected as a volatile variable with EFI_VARIABLE_RUNTIME_ACCESS (systemd v256 boot.c save_selected_entry, efivar_set_raw), so a sufficiently privileged domain can rewrite it at runtime. Only /proc/cmdline is fixed for the boot.
(c) /proc/cmdline is saved_command_line. It can include bootconfig kernel keys and init arguments, so kernelCmdline must be that text, not the entry's options line. Also, systemd-boot adds no BOOT_IMAGE=, which is a GRUB convention, yet the positive pairs a GRUB-shaped command line with a systemd-boot entry ID.
(d) The lockdown check is a token test. 'lockdown=integrity' after '--' is ACCEPTED, but parse_args stops at '--', so the token there goes to init. The observed hardening.lockdown const still covers the actual state.
'The boot entry can' tell the boots apart holds for a non-adversarial maintenance boot whose entries match the record. That is enough under K1's 'trusted installer' alternative.
findings.requiredChange: Qualify the K1 statement as above: declared entries, a runtime-writable entry ID, and /proc/cmdline as the command-line source. Optionally pin the maintenance-selecting token: present in MAINTENANCE, absent in ENROLLED. Make the positive command line consistent with the named loader.

findings.finding: Two points. (1) 'Any cgroup program effective on a process in the slice is effective at its role cgroup' holds for task-selected types: DEVICE, SYSCTL and LSM current. Socket-attached types (INGRESS/EGRESS, SOCK_OPS, sock_addr, sockopt, LSM sock and socket) select by the socket's creation cgroup, sk_cgrp_data, in kernel/bpf/cgroup.c. A socket a role holds but did not create in its role cgroup is outside the census: systemd socket activation, SCM_RIGHTS, or a socket created before a cgroup move. (2) Decision 3 narrows owner decision E1's 'every planeon cgroup' to role cgroups. The narrowing is sound for processes only if the slice census is complete, which the data cannot check.
findings.requiredChange: Reword the scope sentence to cover sockets created in the role cgroup, and state that descriptors created elsewhere are out of scope (or forbidden by W03). Record decision 3's narrowing where E1 is carried (W02e status and W03/T04). Optionally record the slice's cgroup.stat nr_descendants and require it to equal the census size minus one.

findings.location: qualification.schema.json $defs.backendComponents KUBELET and CONTROLLER_MANAGER apiIdentities; README network-policy agent identity row
findings.finding: Two points. (1) The README says KUBELET may use 'system:node:<node name>' (singular), but the schema admits up to 32 node names. ['system:node:unit-node', 'system:node:other-node', 'system:nodes'] is ACCEPTED in the single-node profile, and no node name is bound to the record. (2) apiIdentities is now a subset of the W02g closure. The W02g fixture runs controllers under per-controller credentials (SC06) whose service accounts are outside the closure: endpointslice-controller, node-controller, ttl-controller and others. So the field cannot be the component's complete identity set. Its meaning (complete or partial) is unstated. The disjointness rule is truly subsumed: the enums are pairwise disjoint, the KUBELET pattern matches no other name, and the model's rule is now unreachable.
findings.requiredChange: Allow at most one system:node: name, or bind it to a record field. State that apiIdentities lists the closure identities a component holds, not all identities it authenticates as.

questionAnswers.Q2:
Mostly yes, with one regression (W2). All 131 v2 negatives and the 4 v2 accepted variants replay under v3 with their pinned refusals; v2 member rows add only threadCount, and Q03 uses a v3 capture. Besides R01's version string, exactly four refusals change, each correctly:
- R70: SCHEDULER takes the kubelet's name, so the schema enum fires first.
- R71: DATASTORE has maxItems 0.
- L13: deleting the slice root meets the parent rule first.
- Q07: rewording only.
The identity-disjointness rule is truly subsumed: no enum name is shared, the KUBELET pattern matches no other component's name, and the model rule is now unreachable. P4's restructure is at least as strong as v2's two checks, because inspected processes are members.
The regression: v2's migration guarantees against v1 history no longer hold. A v1-only host can enroll v3 on its v1 boot with v1 nonces, and v1 nonces can be reused after a v2 history (W2).
Legitimate hosts:
- A05, A06 and A07 are accepted, and so is an unpopulated sibling named with a role-cgroup prefix.
- A worker with an unreaped child is refused (W5).
- A maintenance entry that differs only by initrd or UKI, with an identical command line, is refused by design.
- A complete apiIdentities list is impossible for an SC06 controller-manager (W8).
questionAnswers.Q3:
All four kernel facts hold in v6.12. The four cited digests match the published tag files.
- Attach types: to_cgroup_bpf_attach_type maps 28 types, plus BPF_LSM_CGROUP, giving 29. The uapi enum has exactly 29 cgroup attach types, and bpf_prog_query sends all 29 to cgroup_bpf_prog_query. The 22 census types and 7 hooks are disjoint and their union equals that set.
- Effective query: __cgroup_bpf_query with BPF_F_QUERY_EFFECTIVE reads cgrp->bpf.effective. compute_effective_progs includes an ancestor's programs when the ancestor has BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI, and also when no nearer program exists. For BPF_LSM_CGROUP the query loops CGROUP_LSM_START..CGROUP_LSM_END, which is CGROUP_LSM_NUM = 10 slots with CONFIG_BPF_LSM and 0 without it.
- pids.current: it is the pids counter, charged in pids_can_fork, which cgroup_can_fork calls for every copy_process including CLONE_THREAD. It is uncharged in release_task through pids_release. So it counts tasks, including unreaped zombies (W5).
- /proc/<pid>/exe: exec_binprm replaces bprm->file with bprm->interpreter, begin_new_exec calls set_mm_exe_file(bprm->file), and proc_exe_link returns mm->exe_file, so it names the interpreter. Replacing the link needs CAP_SYS_RESOURCE (PR_SET_MM_EXE_FILE), and only after the old file is unmapped; no role holds that capability.
Socket-attached types select by the socket's cgroup (W7).

reviewLimit:
This is a source-level, DATA_CHECK_ONLY review of commit bcd64ee's five subject files. They were hash-verified at the start and the end of the review, and the predecessor inputs were hash-verified at the start.
It establishes no native qualification, and no kernel, SELinux, cgroup, BPF, boot-loader or TPM behaviour. It establishes no installed profile, selected distribution, seccomp filter or E01-E12 obligation, and it authorizes nothing.
The kernel facts come from reading v6.12 source, not from running a kernel; the systemd-boot facts come from systemd v256 source.
Repository tests and validators were not run. The v3 model was imported and executed read-only, through my own replay harness in /private/tmp/claude-501/w02af-review1/. The v2 model was diffed but not executed.
During the review, out-of-subject mechanical edits appeared in the working tree: 123 modified files, including the catalog line of scripts/validate_proxy_contract.py, plus untracked scripts/validate_native_profile_v3.py and tests/test_native_profile_v3.py. They were not reviewed or run.
Only paths in the repository and my scratch directory were accessed. No GitHub, runner, sudo, cloud or warm-source action was taken.
